title: Priority sampler and ops evidence curator for PagerDuty/Slack alerts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Our current PagerDuty and Slack alert attachments often include full traces and logs by default, which results in noisy notifications, large payloads, and slow operator triage. This ticket implements a severity-driven telemetry sampler and evidence curator that selects and formats a compact set of artifacts (trace spans, error logs, metric slices) for inclusion in PD/Slack notifications and seeds an auto-generated postmortem draft when the incident is resolved.

Goals:
- Reduce PD/Slack notification payloads by sampling and prioritizing the most relevant telemetry for triage.
- Surface a ranked evidence bundle (top spans, top error logs, metric deltas) with links to full traces/dashboard.
- Auto-seed a postmortem draft (title, timeline bullets, affected routes, and initial hypothesis) into Confluence/Draft when an incident is marked P1 or requires on-call follow-up.
- Honor privacy/KMS rules: do not forward user PII or raw payloads; only include anonymized IDs and pointers.

Acceptance criteria:
1) PagerDuty alerts for severity >= critical include a curated evidence bundle (max 5 spans, 3 log snippets, 2 metric slices) and a short triage summary.
2) Slack incident thread message includes the same curated bundle and 1-click actions (open trace, run rollback playbook, add to postmortem).
3) Evidence size is capped to 64KB per notification; large artifacts are replaced with links to the full artifact in the telemetry console.
4) Postmortem draft is created for incidents that hit SLO breach AND are acknowledged > 10 minutes; draft includes pre-filled sections and links to the evidence bundle.
5) Feature is behind a feature flag for % rollout and can be disabled at org or route level.

Design/implementation notes:
- Use a sampling policy that weights spans by error-rate, latency delta, and unique service hops.
- Implement an evidence curator microservice (stateless) that consumes a telemetry envelope from the alerting pipeline, runs heuristics and ML scoring, and outputs a compact JSON summary and pointer URLs.
- Integrate curator output into existing alert adapters for PagerDuty and Slack. The adapter will attach the curated bundle and produce a short summary card.
- Use existing SLO store for severity thresholds and to decide postmortem eligibility.
- Add audit log entries for every attachment sent (artifact pointers, curator hash) to satisfy compliance.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: enable for internal monitoring team (10% of alerts) for 2 weeks.
- Monitor false-negatives: incidents where curator omitted the root-cause span; target < 2% during canary.
- Gradual ramp to 50% then org-wide if metrics are stable.

Testing:
- Unit tests for sampler heuristics and size capping.
- E2E with synthetic incidents (latency, OOM, auth-errors) to verify bundle quality.
- Load test to ensure curator maintains sub-100ms processing for alert envelopes at production throughput.

Privacy/security:
- Strip or hash user-identifiable fields per KMS policy before including in attachments.
- Only include pre-approved log fields; any new field must pass a privacy review.

Operational hooks:
- Metrics emitted: curator_processing_time_ms, evidence_bundle_size_bytes, omitted_artifact_count, curator_score_distribution.
- Alerts if curator_processing_time_ms p95 > 250ms or omitted_artifact_count spikes > 5% of alerts.
